summary.title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?

setting_and_object.category: Benchmark (plus evaluation formulation and an accompanying context-engineering method)

details: Existing abstention research treats abstention as a single-turn answer-or-abstain choice, ignoring that a tool-using agent can also keep acting, and that infeasibility may only surface after interacting with the environment.
Key unmeasured failure mode: agents that abstain far too late (many wasted tool calls) or never, versus over-abstaining on solvable tasks.

Agentic Abstention: a formulation of stopping-under-uncertainty as a POMDP with action space {ANSWER, ABSTAIN, ACT}, where each abstain-warranted instance is annotated with the earliest step w_i at which abstention becomes warranted.

A ~28k-instance benchmark built by adapting existing environments into two new abstention types: Request-based (instruction itself rewritten to be infeasible/ambiguous) and Environment-based (instruction unchanged, environment altered so infeasibility is only discoverable through interaction).
Timing-aware metrics: AbsRec@K (abstain within K steps of w_i), timely recall (abstain exactly at w_i), SPL-style path-length-penalized abstention score, and over-abstention rate.

CONVOLVE: a context-engineering method that reflects over full interaction trajectories and curates them into an evolving playbook of reusable stopping rules appended to the agent's context, with no parameter updates.

WebShop: 500 original solvable instructions plus 500 new abstain-warranted ones — 249 request-based rewrites (Subjective Preference, Underspecified Intent, False Premise/Contradiction) generated by GPT-5.4-mini and manually reviewed, and 251 Environment-based 'Missing Target' tasks made by deleting ground-truth items and rebuilding the Lucene index.

Terminal-Bench 2.0: 277 instances (89 solvable, 188 unsolvable); request-based rewrites via a rewriting-agent/validation-agent loop (87 False Premise, 80 Underspecified Intent) plus 21 hand-built 'Missing Prerequisite' environment modifications (removed file, dependency, permission, service).

QA: 16 AbstentionBench datasets (27,073 samples), excluding search-resolvable ones (FreshQA, MuSiQue, SQuAD 2.0, QASPER, CoCoNot-Temporal); converted to sequential answer/abstain/search with a Wikipedia enwiki-20260101 corpus, E5-base dense retrieval, top-3 docs per call, max 10 searches.
Clarification requests are counted as abstention; max 10 turns; timely = AbsRec@1 for request-based, AbsRec@2 for environment-based.
13 LLM-as-agent systems including GPT-5.4-mini, Grok 4.1 Fast, Llama-3.3 8B/70B, GPT-OSS-120B, MiniMax-M2.5, Qwen3 8B/14B/32B/235B-A22B (Instruct and Thinking), Gemma-4-31B-it, GLM-5.1.
Scaffolds: Terminus 2 and Codex CLI, compared with GPT-5.4-mini fixed as base model on Terminal-Bench.
Scenario-specific coverage: WebShop as the main 8-model cross-comparison; QA with 5 models; Terminal for scaffold and reasoning-effort (low/medium/high) comparison.
Instantiated on the WebShop abstention-only subset: 20 training trajectories, 8 validation, 101 held-out eval, stratified by scenario and grouped by original shopping goal.

One offline epoch, at most two reflection/update rounds per example, playbook curated after each example; rollout/reflection capped at 1024 tokens, curator at 512, playbook budget 80k tokens with deterministic 6k-token curator input truncation.
Reflection model identifies which observation made abstention warranted and which actions delayed it; curator converts this into structured add-operations into fixed playbook sections.

Baselines: same base model without playbook, and an in-context-learning variant; cross-size transfer tested (8B lessons into 70B and vice versa); additional runs on AbstentionBench and TerminalBench in appendix.

key_findings.finding: Timely abstention is the dominant failure mode: agents often eventually recognize infeasibility but only after many wasted interactions.
key_findings.evidence: All tested models achieve under 40% average timely recall; most sit in 0.0-0.3 AbsRec@1 across web, terminal and QA. In WebShop the strongest baseline reaches 26.7% AbsRec@1 but 83.2% AbsRec@10; the best terminal configuration reaches only 21.6% timely recall. Six of eight web models, both terminal scaffolds, and four of five QA models stay below 0.5 abstention recall even at 10 turns.

key_findings.finding: Environment-based abstention (infeasibility revealed only after interacting) is markedly harder than request-based abstention, and difficulty varies sharply by category.
key_findings.evidence: In WebShop, False Premise is the easiest request-based category while Missing Target is hardest; in Terminal, Underspecified Intent is hardest for both scaffolds; in QA, Answer Unknown is easiest while False Premise and Underspecified Intent stay at or below ~50% for all models.

key_findings.finding: CONVOLVE substantially improves timely abstention without parameter updates, and lessons distilled by a small model transfer to a large one.
key_findings.evidence: On the 101-example WebShop held-out set, Llama-3.3-70B with its own playbook rises from 26.7 to 57.4 AbsRec@1, 83.2 to 100.0 AbsRec@10, and 55.3 to 78.9 SPL, using only 20 training trajectories; using an 8B-derived playbook the 70B model reaches nearly the same (55.3 / 99.0 / 76.4). Gains replicate on AbstentionBench (25.0 to 39.7 AbsRec@1) and TerminalBench (37.6 to 68.9 AbsRec@1).

key_findings.finding: Neither scale nor more reasoning reliably improves timely abstention, and they can trade off against overall abstention.
key_findings.evidence: Across Qwen3 8B/14B/32B/235B on WebShop, larger models raise overall recall but timely recall changes only slightly; Qwen3-235B-Thinking improves timely recall but lowers AbsRec@10 relative to Instruct; for GPT-5.4-mini on Terminal, medium reasoning is best and high reasoning brings no further gain.

key_findings.finding: The agent scaffold, independent of the base model, materially shapes abstention behavior.
key_findings.evidence: With GPT-5.4-mini fixed, Codex CLI reaches ~0.38 AbsRec@10 on Terminal-Bench versus ~0.18 for Terminus 2, and outperforms it at all values of K and across abstention categories.
